get.description:
Retrieves latest DECOR transaction or dataset tree based on transaction id (oid). If multiple are found based on the id, then the latest is returned based on effectiveDate, regardless of its status. If you omit the `treeonly` query parameter or set it to false, you get the metadata of the transaction. If the transaction is a group you also get the leaf transactions and their metadata. For each leaf you get the bare representingTemplate with its concepts.

If you need access to the expanded representingTemplate, i.e. the list of concepts attached to this transaction with names and other properties, use `treeonly=true`. The object you get back from that no longer is the transaction but actually the dataset attached to the transaction, trimmed down to the concepts mentioned in the representingTemplate.

Finally when going into edit mode, you would want the full dataset in scope so you are able to pick and choose from concepts formerly not present in the representingTemplate. Use `treeonly=true&fulltree=true` to get all concepts where absent concepts are marked with property `absent: "true"`

post.description:
Get a dataset concept ready for editing. There are a couple of different scenarios. Each concept is always retrieved fully expanded, but with any `inherit` (indicator of a designcopy) and `contains` (indicator of a containment) in place, and a few extras:
1. Element `lock`. This is your ticket towards saving the result later on. Without a lock you cannot save
1. Element `edit`. This marks the concept as *updated*
1. Element `move`. This marks the concept as *moved*
1. Element(s) `terminologyAssociation` and/or `identifierAssociation` as convenience so you know what the connections were upon requesting to edit

When you save the dataset, only concepts with a marker `edit` or `move` are considered for updating. The `lock` is checked for on the server so no dependency there. 

Please consider the following scenarios:
1. Edit of a concept item or group
    1. Example call `concept/[id]/[effective date]/$edit`
1. Edit of concept with a request to let it be a designcopy (inherit) from a specific target concept
    1. Example call `concept/[id]/[effective date]/$edit?targetType=designcopy&targetId=[id]&targetEffectiveDate=[effective date]`
1. Edit of concept with a request to let it be a containment (contains) of a specific target concept
    1. Example call `concept/[id]/[effective date]/$edit?targetType=containment&targetId=[id]&targetEffectiveDate=[effective date]`
1. Edit of concept that currently is a containment of some other concept by converting it into a designcopy of that same concept
    1. Example call `concept/[id]/[effective date]/$edit?targetType=to-designcopy`
1. Edit of concept that currently is a designcopy (inherit) of some other concept by converting it into a true copy of that same concept
    1. Example call `concept/[id]/[effective date]/$edit?targetType=to-copy`

The following additional thing may be used:
1. `breakLock` - you cannot go into edit mode without a lock, but someone might have left one, blocking you access. If you know this lock to be stale, potentially after conversing with the owner, you may use breakLock=true to override that lock with your own. **NOTE** There's no undo for this.
1. `generateConceptListIds` - when you use `targetType=to-copy` you are creating a copy of the concept. By default however you keep referring to the original conceptList (if any), and so any terminology associations keep connected to the original conceptList and conceptList concepts (again, if any). This is convenient, but is also in the way of you associating your own terminology associations. Any connections would immediately also apply to the original. If that is not what you want/need then use generateConceptListIds=true to have fresh ids generated on your conceptLists and conceptList concepts. The result will also include copies of the old terminology associations under the new id as a base, but you may replace/delete those at will before or after saving the dataset.

200.description: Return data as normal for a concept that does inherit/containment

parameters.description: parameter denoting the id of the source concept
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: parameter denoting the effectiveDate of the source concept
parameters.name: effectiveDate

parameters.description: parameter denoting the id of the target concept
parameters.name: targetId

parameters.description: parameter denoting the effectiveDate of the target concept. If not given assumes latest version for id
parameters.name: targetEffectiveDate

parameters.description:
parameter denoting a specific action to apply to the concept under `id` and `effectiveDate`. Without this option, `targetId` and `targetEffectiveDate` are ignored and concept is returned for editing without further action. Options

* `designcopy` - requires a value for `targetId` and optionally `targetEffectiveDate` pointing to an existing other concept. To avoid circular references, this target concept shall not be a parent or child of the source concept. This option creates a counterpart under the source concept using an `inherit` node signifying which concept it references.
* `containment` - requires a value for `targetId` and optionally `targetEffectiveDate` pointing to an existing other concept. Contrary to `designcopy` this may be a parent or child node of the source concept. This option creates a `contains` node under the source concept which acts as a _hyperlink_ into the target concept.
* `to-designcopy` - requires the source concept under `id` and `effectiveDate` to be a containment. This option acts as if the values for concept.contains are the `targetId` and `targetEffectiveDate` and `targetType` has value `designcopy`. It effectively turns a containment into a designcopy. See above for further description. Again to avoid circular references, the inherit recursion stops at every level where the target concept is a containment.
* `to-copy` - requires the source concept under `id` and `effectiveDate` to be a design copy or containment. This option makes a copy of the target concept tree. Each concept in the tree has a relationship to the concept it is a copy of. See parameter `generateConceptListIds` for further details

If you want a full copy with new unique ids on conceptList and any underlying conceptList.concepts you may set this parameters value to `true`.

patch.description:
Patches an existing implementation guide. Expect as input array of parameter objects, each containing RFC 6902 compliant contents.
For paages:
* adding/moving - use `"op": "replace"`, `"path": "/pages"`, and as `"value"` send the page tree with the pages in the desired order, and new pages in the desired spot. The page tree MAY have added pages, and SHALL contain all existing pages. Use GET /implementationguide/{id}/{effectiveDate}/pages to obtain the current full tree. New pages are recognized because their id will not exist yet. The format of the new id is not important on input: it will be replaced by a new uuid on output. It is not possible to override the id of a page. Title is stored from input. Contents and subpages are merged in from the stored version the page, except for new pages.
* updating - use `"op": "remove"`, `"path": "/page"`, and as `"value"` send the page to be updated. the title and contents of the page that matches the id will be updated. Any subpages are merged in from the stored page
* deleting - use `"op": "remove"`, `"path": "/page"`, and as `"value"` send the page to be deleted. The page that matches the id _with all its children_ will be deleted

* ig - (default) return full implementation guide as-is comparable to /implementationguide/{id}/{effectiveDate}
* metadata - return implementation guide metadata which is all except the definition comparable to /implementationguide/{id}/{effectiveDate}/metadata
* page - return the page you are patching. Can only be used if one and only one page is patched based on the input parameters
* pages - return page tree comparable to /implementationguide/{id}/{effectiveDate}/pages
* resources - return resource list comparable to /implementationguide/{id}/{effectiveDate}/resources
parameters.name: returnmode

put.description:
Updates an existing concept. Properties `id`, and `effectiveDate` SHALL match in the requestBody and cannot be updated. 

* concept item: replaces the existing concept with the contents of the concept in requestBody. Special attention things:
  * SHALL have a `valueDomain` with a supported type
  * SHALL have a `conceptList` if `valueDomain` is of type _code_
  * SHALL refer to an existing conceptList in the same project if `conceptList.ref`
  * SHALL be a server unique `conceptList.id` if it does not match the existing _conceptList.id_ for the concept
  * SHALL NOT change existing `conceptList.id` if there are still references to the existing _id_
  * SHALL be a server unique `conceptList.concept.id` if it does not match the existing `conceptList.concept.id` for the concept
  * Any terminology associations on the existing `conceptList.id` and/or `conceptList.concept.id` have to be reestablished after saving an updated concept that changes ids of any of these
* concept group: replaces the existing concept with the contents of the concept in requestBody. Special attention things:
  * the requestBody concept SHOULD NOT specify any child concepts. These are simply taken from the existing, stored concept
  * Exception: if the updated concept has inherited from a different concept than the stored concvept, then the updated concept will overwrite any stored, existing child concepts

  **Note** that it is not possible to delete or move any child concepts this way (exception for new inherits under a group). Please see patch for statusCode updates, move and delete. Concepts may live in datasets or transactions: presence of the parameter `transactionId` and `transactionEffectiveDate` indicates which is applicable.

Retrieves latest or all versions of (pseudo) DECOR codeSystem based on id or name. Latest version, regardless of status, is the default while 'versions=true' returns all versions of a DECOR codeSystem. Id is expected to be an OID.

**NOTE** Not every code system is expressed as a DECOR code system. SNOMED CT and LOINC are examples of systems expressed in a different and incompatible format. When you call such a system it is retreived as a pseudo DECOR codeSystem which follows the same properties for as far as available. The response for non-DECOR systems might be missing effectiveDate and statusCode which are normally present on DECOR codeSystems. The response for non-DECOR systems will never have `.url` or `.ident` or any contents. They only aim to provide meta data about the system.
